root_cause: Escape key in a submenu incorrectly closes all submenus of the root menu instead of only the immediate submenu, causing focus to jump to the wrong menubar item and incorrectly closing parent submenus.
repair_strategy: Modify the Escape handler in menubar.js _handleKeyup for non‑top‑level menus: if the currently focused menu item has an open submenu, close that submenu and keep focus on the item; otherwise close the submenu opened by the parent menu item and move focus to that parent menu item.
expected_accessibility_effect: Escape will close only the innermost open submenu and move focus to its parent menubar item, leaving any parent submenus open as required.
functional_risks: Change may affect other Escape behaviors that relied on closing all submenus; ensure no other parts of the code depend on that behavior.
Focus management must correctly handle nested submenus; incorrect index calculation could misfocus.
Ensure that closing a submenu via Escape does not inadvertently affect sibling submenus or the menubar controller.
verification_requirements: Verify the exact journey steps: Escape on #history returns focus to #facts with #facts aria-expanded false and #about aria-expanded true.
Test Escape on a submenu item that has an open submenu (e.g., #facts) – should close that submenu and keep focus on the item.
Test Escape on a top-level menubar item with an open submenu – should close the submenu and keep focus on the menubar item.
Test Escape when no submenu is open – should leave focus unchanged and not close any submenu.
Confirm that aria‑expanded attributes are updated correctly and that focus is visible after each Escape press.
